The Deesis

Icons

Christ

The Deesis

Deësis · Deisis · Supplication · Intercession

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

1 Timothy 2:1–5

John 5:28–30

John 3:29–30

King James Version · Scripture previews

Fr. Vladimir Berzonsky describes the Deesis as Christ enthroned, flanked by the Mother of God and Saint John the Baptist turning toward Him in prayer. He explains its Greek name through adoration, prayer, and intercession on behalf of human beings.

[1] Opening prose paragraph after the Scripture epigraph

What is depicted

The selected early-eighteenth-century Deesis comes from the iconostasis of a chapel in the Church of St. Elijah the Prophet, Yaroslavl, according to its file description. The three figures occupy a single panel: Christ at the center, Mary and John beside Him.

[2] File description and displayed historic reproduction

History and tradition

The Uffizi’s separate Russian Deesis object illustrates another format: three small panels probably joined as a folding traveling icon. The museum also documents variations in the figures’ posture. The title therefore names a compositional relationship that appears across more than one object format.

[3] Description, paragraphs 1–2

Published explanation

Metropolitan Tikhon likewise identifies Mary and John as the principal intercessors in the Deesis. His published explanation calls John Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist, relating his place beside Christ to the different aspects of his ministry.

[4] Opening paragraph

I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men;

[5] 1 Timothy 2:1
